name: Sew on a button properly
blurb: Twenty minutes to learn, useful for the rest of your life. The detail that separates a proper job from a bodge is the shank — the small gap that lets the button sit over the fabric.
gear: Needle and thread matching the garment
A spare button, or the one that fell off
steps: Thread the needle with about 45 cm of doubled thread and knot the end.
Come up from underneath at the button position and place the button on the needle.
Lay a matchstick or a pin across the top of the button and sew over it, four to six passes through each pair of holes.
Remove the matchstick, bring the needle up between button and fabric, and wind the thread tightly around the threads underneath to form the shank.
Push the needle back through to the underside and finish with two or three small knotted stitches.
Trim and test by doing the button up — it should sit flat without straining.
tips: No shank means a button that puckers the fabric and pops off again in a month.
Four-hole buttons can be sewn as parallel bars or a cross. Match whatever the other buttons on the garment do.
proof: A button you sewed survives a full wash cycle and sits as neatly as the factory ones.
